text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99 exceeded threshold in eu-streaming-api (p99=1.24s, threshold=500ms). Triggered 2026-03-17T10:45:11Z. Link: https://dash.internal/redwood/streams?range=5m :rotating_light:

maya: i'm oncall, joining :phone: logging in to dashboard now

sam: saw it too — p95 up ~2x, p99 spike is concentrated on streaming tail requests (seq len > 1024)

lena: any new deploys in eu?

chao: no deploys in last 45m. infra events show GC churn on a subset of infer nodes and KV cache hit rate dropped sharply around 10:43Z

omar: support: two customers reported session stalls and timeouts in the last 10m (cust-a, cust-b). file refs: #1234, #1237

maya: quick triage checklist: 1) confirm impact (prod sessions) 2) verify recent deploys 3) check kvcache, batching, queue depth 4) consider immediate routing fallback + scale up

sam: pulling metrics: 
```
# last 10m aggregate (eu-streaming-api)
p95: 320ms -> 640ms
p99: 220ms -> 1240ms
kv_cache_hit: 0.12 -> 0.04
inflight_streams_per_node: +45%
error_rate(429/timeout): low but some timeouts on tail requests
```

chao: confirming KV hit drop on nodes: node-eu-12/13/14 show hit ~3-5% vs baseline 30%

lena: could be kv cache eviction after a big prefix churn or cache warmup fail after GC

sam: mitigation options (fast):
- shift 15% traffic to us-west fallback model (lighter)
- scale eu-inference pool +2 nodes now
- force warmup of KV cache for hot prefixes
- temporarily reduce max_seq_length for streaming route (risky)

maya: i'm going to start routing fallback + scale. will coordinate. tagging @chao to run scale

chao: executing scale now: `redwood infra scale --pool eu-inference --add 2 --reason "p99 surge"` ETA ~75s. also kicking a kvcache-warmup job for top prefixes

chao: starting traffic shift: `redwood router update-weight --route /v1/stream --region eu --to-region us-west --weight 15` (canary over 30s)

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff window updated. Incident owner: maya. Pager duty: sam alerted for infra follow-up

sam: checking node logs while scale kicks in — seeing repeated long tail attention kernel stalls on node-eu-13, collecting flame traces

incident-bot: Update: scale request accepted, provisioning 2 instances (req id: rq-8892).

chao: kvcache warmup job started for prefixes: ["/user/session/", "/chat/context/"]

maya: customer comms: omar please send quick ack to the impacted customers: we're investigating and doing traffic mitigation

omar: sending now: "Thanks — we're investigating higher latency for streaming in EU. We've shifted some traffic and are provisioning extra capacity. Will follow up in ~15m."

incident-bot: Metric update (1m): p99 -> 680ms; p95 -> 380ms; kv_cache_hit -> 0.10 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: improvement visible but still >SLO. flame traces show stalled attention step around step 2048 for long sequences. looks like KERNEL_A hotloop stalls on a few GPUs

lena: is it safe to increase the fallback weight more (to 30%) for immediate relief? we'll have degraded quality for some requests but reduce end-user latency

maya: yes do 30% if p99 not under 500ms in next 3m. keep monitoring. also leave scaling running until stable.

chao: increased route to 30% now. scaling completed, 2 new nodes up (node-eu-21/22). warming in progress.

incident-bot: Update: p99 -> 420ms, p95 -> 280ms. error rate stable. :white_check_mark:

maya: nice. leaving postmortem holder: lena. action items: - investigate kv eviction root cause - analyze kernel stalls and push instrumentation - evaluate circuit for long seqs - update runbook to include autoscale thresholds.

omar: I'll update customers in 20m with latest status.

sam: I'll keep a close watch for 30m, ping if anything recurs.

lena: taking postmortem. adding preliminary notes to docs.

maya: closing incident channel in 30m if stable. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
